cases.name: Liza
cases.en: “It is hard to go when nobody can look after my child,” Liza says.
cases.fil: “Mahirap pumunta kapag walang magbabantay sa anak ko,” sabi ni Liza.

cases.name: Jo
cases.en: Jo, 24, is worried about something she heard about family planning.
cases.fil: Si Jo, 24, ay may takot sa narinig tungkol sa family planning.

cases.name: Ben
cases.en: Ben, 37, says he has felt low for several weeks.
cases.fil: Si Ben, 37, ay nagsasabing ilang linggo na siyang malungkot.

cases.name: Ramon
cases.en: “May we discuss smoking and the support you want?” Gibs asks. … “I want to cut down, but it is hard when I am stressed,” Ramon says.
cases.fil: “Puwede ba nating pag-usapan ang paninigarilyo at ang suportang gusto mo?” tanong ni Gibs. … “Gusto kong mabawasan, pero mahirap kapag stress,” sabi ni Ramon.

paragraphs: Gibs hears Liza’s childcare concern. One first step: ask the midwife about scheduling. No appointment is promised.
Jo heard something about family planning and wants to choose for herself. Listen. If she wants, find a qualified contact through the health team. Gibs does not choose a method.

Ben has felt low for weeks and wants someone to talk to. Listen without diagnosing. Identify a qualified contact; the time is unconfirmed. In real immediate danger, do not delay help for an ordinary interview.
Ramon wants to cut down smoking; stress is a barrier. Ask permission and listen. Gibs does not give or choose medicine. Verify a health-team contact and check understanding.
In triads, everyone tries the BHW role. Ask for the step in their own words. Repair misunderstanding and recheck. Peer feedback is practice, not a facilitator grade.

“Do I have an appointment tomorrow?” Liza asks. “Not yet. First we will ask about scheduling,” Gibs clarifies. On recheck, Liza says, “Ask first; no appointment yet.” “Yes, that is the first step,” Gibs confirms.
Walang magbabantay sa anak ni Liza. Magtatanong si Gibs sa midwife tungkol sa iskedyul; wala pang appointment.
Takot si Jo sa narinig tungkol sa family planning; gusto niyang siya ang pumili. Makinig at, kung gusto niya, alamin ang kwalipikadong contact sa health team. Hindi si Gibs ang pipili ng paraan.

Ilang linggo nang malungkot si Ben; gusto niyang may makausap. Makinig nang walang diagnosis. Alamin ang kwalipikadong contact; hindi tiyak ang oras. Sa agarang panganib, humingi agad ng tulong ayon sa lokal na pamamaraan.
Gustong bawasan ni Ramon ang paninigarilyo; hadlang ang stress. Humingi ng pahintulot at makinig. Hindi pipili o magbibigay ng gamot si Gibs. Alamin ang health-team contact at tiyakin ang pagkaunawa.
Sa triad, lahat ay BHW minsan. Ipasabi ang hakbang sa sariling salita, ayusin ang hindi malinaw, at mag-check muli. Pagsasanay ang peer feedback, hindi facilitator grade.

“May appointment na ako bukas?” tanong ni Liza. “Hindi pa. Magtatanong muna tungkol sa iskedyul,” paglilinaw ni Gibs. Sa recheck, sagot ni Liza, “Magtatanong muna; wala pang appointment.” “Tama, iyon muna,” tugon ni Gibs.
